steps.text: Light arrives as photons, each carrying energy E = hf.
Photoelectric effect: one photon can release at most one electron.
Electrons are only emitted when f ≥ f₀ (threshold frequency), whatever the intensity.
hf = Φ + KE_max: photon energy splits between work function and kinetic energy.
Higher intensity means more photons, hence more electrons, but not faster ones.
Line spectra come from discrete energy levels: E₂ − E₁ = hf.
